items.note: The page sets up the recursion (W role streams of volume V/W, one call at parameter f per unit of edge rank, s calls in all), writes the interchange recurrence C(mf) <= (s/W)C(f)+O(1), solves it and shows that the exponent log_m(s/W)=1+log_m(1-eta) is below 1 exactly when eta>0, as in the paper (Prop. power-interchange, eq. swap-recurrence). The complex variant is only partly solved (see S1.6).

Derived from the mechanism: 'A call at parameter mf cuts each chunk into m slots of parameter f', rows are dealt into 'W streams of volume V/W', and 'An edge's frame change costs one call at parameter f on that wire's stream per unit of rank', so 'the call makes s calls at parameter f, each on volume V/W'. This matches the paper's lines 170-174 and 1497-1546, including dividing by volume to get the factor s/W<m.

dropped: every scratch wire is restored whatever its initial value, which is why the scratch roles can carry genuine rows and every stream has volume exactly V/W
items.note: The page only refers to the 'exchange network' (linked) and says that the W streams are 'one per wire of the bit or complex network'. It never states what the network computes or that it restores the scratch wires.

dropped: the same frame D_v on all incidences of a gate, so that it commutes with the pointwise gates
items.note: Stated as 'Each vertex carries a frame, a reversible re-encoding of a wire's array; since a route applies only its two endpoint frames, the network applies the intended operation to every row', with a link.

The page sketches the count the way the paper does (lines 1066-1071, 1162-1167): baseline Wm, a saving of 2N because X_a starts on a line and Y_a ends on an (m-1)-space, plus 2L to regain the dimensions lost, plus one rank per bit source sign. This gives s_b=W_b m-(N-2L_b) and s_c=W_c m-(2N-2L_c). The values L/N=100/539 and 101/539 are cited, not derived, which is appropriate for an other-page step.

The full chain is given: 'm^{1-2^{-50}}=m exp(-2^{-50} ln m)>m(1-2^{-50} ln m)>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta)=s/W for either network', hence s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. This is the paper's argument (lines 1319-1344), with the tangent-line step made explicit.

eta_b=(N-2L_b)/(W_b m) with W_b=(22587335/539)N gives 339/22587335000000 (checked exactly). eta_c=(2N-2L_c)/(W_c m)=73/19906842167500 is correct, but W_c is not given, so the reader cannot recompute that value. The paper only displays the two values.
'Both exceed 20*2^{-50}~1.8*10^{-14}, by a factor over 200': the decimal values 1.5e-11 and 3.7e-12 make the comparison checkable. The ratios are about 845 and 206.
'Since m=10^6<2^20 and ln 2<1, ln m<20', as in the paper.
The chain is reproduced and justified by 'the exponential lies above its tangent at 0'. It then uses ln m<20 and 20*2^{-50}<eta.
Since s/W=m(1-eta), the chain gives s/W<m^{1-2^{-50}} for both networks, with 0<tau=sigma<1.

dropped: extension from power widths e=m^k to arbitrary widths (base-m decomposition of the width)
rows supplied by high digits so the row count is divisible by W^k
padding of binary chunks of u bits to radix-q ranges, giving O(Vu^tau)
items.note: For power widths the page derives the bit-variant recurrence and its solution, as in the paper's Prop. power-interchange: 'C(mf)<=(s/W)C(f)+O(1), C(1)=O(1)', the geometric sum, 'an interchange costs O(Vf^tau)'. The general u-bit statement is left to the linked page.

dropped: the leaf contribution a^j u <= e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}, which is the source of the sigma+beta(1-sigma) term
the overhead bound (eK)^tau=O(e^lambda), which uses K<=d^c<=e^{c/beta} at internal nodes and the conditions max{tau,sigma}<lambda, tau(1+c/beta)<lambda
beta=1/2 and the definition of lambda
the row preprocessing on the first q_0 chunks and the base-m split of D-q_0
items.note: The layer recurrence 'C(f)<=(s/W)C(f/m)+O((fK)^tau+1), C(f)=O(f) (f<d^beta)' matches the paper (line 2407). The solution is only asserted: 'the overheads again sum geometrically, and the simultaneous butterfly layer costs O(Vd^{lambda'})'.

errors.quote: The branching factor is the fixed label-space dimension $m=h^3=10^6$ of the exchange network
errors.problem: m is the factor by which the parameter shrinks per level, not the branching factor. Each call has s children, and the paper says 'the branching factor s is fixed and the depth is at most ceil(log_m d)'. The page later uses s correctly.

errors.quote: A call at parameter $mf$ cuts each chunk into $m$ slots of parameter $f$, one per coordinate of the label space.
errors.problem: This holds only for interchange, where each of the two chunks becomes m fields of e/m digits. For the layer, whose parameter counts axes, the paper splits the e active chunks into m slots of e/m chunks each; it does not cut each chunk.

errors.quote: its frame changes are binary changes of basis, done by chunk interchanges at cost $O(V((fK)^\tau+1))$ per node
errors.problem: The frame changes along edges are the recursive layer calls, one per residual basis vector, as the page itself said earlier. The node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)) consists of the binary changes of basis around them (row additions by the packed selected-bit lemma), their inverses, scalar gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly (paper lines 2289-2296).
